Competencies

Show indicators at

Showing the L3 indicator for each competency. Open a competency to see all five levels.

  • Descriptive statistics6.3.1

    L1 Awareness

    Recognise mean, median, variance, quantiles, frequency tables, and when each is appropriate.

    L2 Familiarity

    Produce a basic descriptive table for a pharma dataset following a template.

    L3 Proficiency

    Produce regulatory-grade descriptive summaries (Table 1, baseline characteristics, AE summaries) for real pharma data.

    L4 Mastery

    Tailor descriptive analysis to the audience and decision; spot non-trivial issues hiding in summary statistics.

    L5 Expertise

    Does not apply at this level. further mastery folds into other Statistics competencies

  • Variability, uncertainty, sampling error, and inference6.3.2

    L1 Awareness

    Recognise variability and sampling error as distinct from systematic error.

    L2 Familiarity

    Compute and report SEs and CIs on a small pharma sample following examples.

    L3 Proficiency

    Quantify and communicate uncertainty in real pharma analyses appropriately.

    L4 Mastery

    Handle non-trivial uncertainty (clustered, time-varying, hierarchical, Bayesian).

    L5 Expertise

    Set the team's standards for reporting uncertainty.

  • Basic probability theory and randomness6.3.3

    L1 Awareness

    Recognise probability concepts: events, conditional probability, independence, distributions.

    L2 Familiarity

    Compute basic probabilities and simulate random draws following examples.

    L3 Proficiency

    Apply probability reasoning fluently to pharma analyses (risk, hazard, predictive distributions).

    L4 Mastery

    Reason about non-trivial probability structures in pharma data (joint, hierarchical, censored).

    L5 Expertise

    Contribute methods or coach the team.

  • Hypothesis testing6.3.4

    L1 Awareness

    Recognise null/alternative hypotheses, type I/II error, p-values, confidence intervals.

    L2 Familiarity

    Run a basic test (t, χ², simple regression) on a pharma sample following an example.

    L3 Proficiency

    Choose and interpret hypothesis tests honestly for real pharma questions (effect sizes, CIs, multiplicity).

    L4 Mastery

    Handle non-trivial pharma testing (group sequential, multiple endpoints, non-inferiority, Bayesian).

    L5 Expertise

    Set the team's standards for hypothesis testing.

  • Statistical modeling (incl. regression) and model assessment6.3.5

    L1 Awareness

    Recognise regression and modelling as a way to relate variables under uncertainty.

    L2 Familiarity

    Fit a linear/logistic regression on a pharma sample following an example.

    L3 Proficiency

    Build and assess real pharma models (GLM, mixed-effects, GAM, survival) with appropriate diagnostics.

    L4 Mastery

    Handle non-trivial modelling — hierarchical, longitudinal, joint, missing-data — with credible assumptions and assessment.

    L5 Expertise

    Set the team's modelling standards or contribute to methods.

  • Design of experiments (DOE). Nonsampling error, biases, confounding, and causal inference6.3.6

    L1 Awareness

    Recognise the difference between sampling and non-sampling error; recognise confounding and bias as concepts.

    L2 Familiarity

    Read a DOE / RCT design and explain its logic.

    L3 Proficiency

    Apply DOE principles and standard bias/confounding adjustments to real pharma analyses.

    L4 Mastery

    Lead complex pharma study design — adaptive trials, factorial DOE, target trial emulation — and reason rigorously about non-sampling error.

    L5 Expertise

    Set the team's design standards or contribute methods.

Pharma examples

Each example is tagged with the competency and level it shows. Tags open that level.

  • A descriptive table that meets ICH E9 expectations for a CSRDescriptive statistics L3
  • A prespecified hypothesis test for a primary trial endpoint with multiplicity adjustmentHypothesis testing L3
  • A mixed-effects model with sensible random structure for repeated measuresStatistical modeling (incl. regression) and model assessment L4
  • A factorial DOE for a process-development study with proper randomisationDesign of experiments (DOE)... L4

Typical stack

R (stats, tidymodels, survival, lme4, brms, rstanarm), Python (statsmodels, pingouin, pymc); design-of-experiments tooling.
